01 / UNDERSTAND THE TASK

One image. More than one finding.

Multi-label classification asks fourteen separate yes/no questions. It does not force one winning diagnosis.

Reported · task

NIH ChestX-ray14; 14 outputs; DenseNet-121-based reproduction and DannyNet, plus a ViT comparison.

Build a hypothetical label vector

These switches illustrate label encoding. They are not predictions or a clinical case. All zeros means no listed finding is labeled, not proof of a healthy patient.

From pixels to independent scores

Image

Feature extractor

14 sigmoids

Each sigmoid maps a logit to a score between 0 and 1. Scores do not need to sum to 1: findings can coexist.

Hypothetical scores:Effusion 0.72Atelectasis 0.61

Multi-class softmax instead distributes one unit of score across mutually exclusive classes. That is a different task.

03 / A FAIR TEST

Keep the patient on one side.

Several images can come from one person. Splitting images at random can place related observations in both training and testing.

Simulation · six hypothetical patients
Train: update weights
→
Validation: choose settings
→
Test: final assessment

Report the unit of splitting, tune thresholds on validation data, and preserve the test set for final assessment. Patient independence does not by itself prove external generalization.

04 / WHY A BACKBONE?

Reuse learned features. Change the head.

A pretrained network provides a starting point. Fine-tuning adapts its parameters to the new task.

Dense connections

Schematic · not 121 displayed layers

Later layers receive earlier feature maps through concatenation. This supports feature reuse; a connecting line is not a new disease prediction.

DenseNet paper ↗

Three distinct ideas

Transfer learning
Start from weights learned on another task; replace the classifier and fine-tune.
Vision Transformer
Represent image patches as tokens and use attention to combine information. Architecture alone does not determine performance.
Augmentation
Alter training images while intending to preserve their labels. Each transformation needs domain justification.
1.00× brightness

This is a separate teaching image from the small lab, not the paper’s training data. Brightness changes here do not retrain a model or demonstrate a performance benefit.

05 / WHAT DOES THE MODEL LEARN FROM?

Give hard examples more attention.

Compare cross-entropy with focal loss while changing confidence and the focusing parameter.

Formula explorer · α fixed at 1
BCE = −log(pₜ)
Focal = (1−pₜ)ᵞ × BCE

γ = 0 recovers BCE here. Larger γ suppresses easy-example loss; this is not automatic rare-class weighting and can emphasize mislabeled hard examples too.

Separate the moving parts

Loss
Defines the penalty for a prediction.
Optimizer
Uses gradients to update parameters. AdamW applies weight decay separately from its adaptive update.
Scheduler
Changes the learning rate during training.
Decision threshold
Converts a score into a yes/no decision after inference.

The paper describes trying individual changes, but does not tabulate their ablation results. Ask for those comparisons before attributing improvement to one component.

06 / RANKING IS NOT A DECISION

High AUC. Low F1. Both can be true.

Move the threshold on an invented set of predictions. The ranking stays fixed while the decisions change.

Synthetic scores · not the paper’s ROC curve or predictions
● Positive label○ Negative labelVertical line: threshold
AUC
Precision
Recall
F1

AUC: probability that a randomly chosen positive receives a higher score than a negative, with half credit for ties. It does not specify sensitivity at a particular threshold.

F1: 2TP ÷ (2TP + FP + FN). It combines precision and recall at a chosen threshold and ignores true negatives.

One threshold or one per finding?

Three invented label tasks

The class-specific values were chosen for this teaching example. In a real experiment, choose them on validation data. Macro averaging gives each class equal weight; micro averaging pools counts.

Rare findings and false alarms

Hypothetical cohort · 1,000 people

Keep sensitivity and specificity fixed at 90%. Change prevalence and watch precision change.

Real sensitivity and specificity may also change between populations. This calculation isolates prevalence only.

07 / EXPLANATION AND CALIBRATION

Ask what a picture—or a score—proves.

Grad-CAM: class-specific attribution

Grad-CAM weights feature maps using gradients for a chosen class, combines them, and retains positive contributions. Its coarse map depends on the class and chosen layer.

Synthetic pattern—not a real Grad-CAM result. A highlighted region is not lesion ground truth or evidence that a diagnosis is correct.

Grad-CAM method ↗

Calibration: does 0.8 behave like 80%?

For observations assigned a score near 0.8, inspect how often the label is actually positive. Ranking, threshold performance, and calibration answer different questions.

Invented example. A lower focal-loss number does not substitute for a reliability diagram, calibration metric, or external evaluation.

08 / PUT THE EVIDENCE TOGETHER

What can you conclude?

A critical reader checks the measurement, the comparison, and what remains untested.

Companion interpretation
Threshold policies differ

Only DannyNet uses class-specific F1 thresholds in this comparison. Ask how all models perform after the same validation-based tuning procedure.

Loss is not calibration

The objectives differ. Ask for calibration curves and suitable calibration metrics before interpreting lower loss as more reliable scores.

Original-study comparison has limits

Check identical splits, labels, and preprocessing. Distinguish an architectural reproduction from reproducing a radiologist comparison.

Class results matter

Read the selected disease row, not just the mean. Missing values stay missing; do not invent a confusion matrix from AUC and F1.

Uncertainty matters

Ask for repeated seeds, class sample counts, confidence intervals, controlled ablations, and external evaluation.

Keep projects distinct

This guide displays reported results and simulations. The 28×28 lab is a separate binary pediatric experiment; its AUC cannot be ranked directly against a 14-label benchmark.
